title: Low-degree local-cohomology algebraization in a complete local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for the maximal-ideal adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $I\subsetneq A$ be an ideal and let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an ideal $K$, put $\Gamma_K(N)=\{x\in N:K^r x=0\text{ for some }r\geq0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], and write $R\Gamma_K$ for its right derived functor and $H_K^j(M)=H^j(R\Gamma_K(M[0]))$. Write $L^{\wedge_I}=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ for derived $I$-adic completion: the derived tensor is computed using a K-flat resolution, and the derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] using the mapping fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the termwise products of a complex-level model of the tower. Use these derived-functor models and their natural completion maps, not arbitrary maps between abstract choices of cones. Fix an integer $q\geq0$ such that $H_I^j(N)=0$ for every $A$-module $N$ and every $j>q$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ not containing $I$ with $V(\mathfrak p)\cap V(I)\ne\{\mathfrak m\}$ assume $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq1$ or $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}+\dim\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)>q+1$, using regular-sequence depth [def-weil-pbc-depth], localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Here $V(K)=\{\mathfrak p:K\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then there exists an ideal $J_0$ with $V(J_0)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$ such that, for every ideal $J\subseteq J_0$ with $V(J)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, the canonical composite $\alpha_J:R\Gamma_J(M[0])\longrightarrow(R\Gamma_J(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}\cong(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}$ induces isomorphisms on $H^0$ and $H^1$. The displayed identification is the natural one from equality of supports after intersecting with $V(I)$.
